title: Frothy Whisked Matcha Green Tea
summary: Sifted matcha is whisked to a paste with a little 80 °C water, then whisked briskly with the rest until covered in fine green foam.
equipment: fine tea strainer or small sieve
bamboo matcha whisk (chasen) or small milk frother

steps.title: Warm the bowls
steps.text: Pour some hot water into each bowl to warm it, then pour it away and dry the whisk. Let the 140 ml water cool to 80 °C; boiling water makes matcha bitter.

steps.title: Sift
steps.text: Sift 2 g matcha into each bowl to break up any lumps.

steps.title: Make a paste
steps.text: Add 15 ml of the water to each bowl and whisk gently into a smooth paste with no dry spots.

steps.title: Whisk to a froth
steps.text: Add the remaining water, about 55 ml per bowl, and whisk briskly in a zigzag 'M' motion from the wrist for 20-30 seconds, until covered in fine, pale green foam. Lift the whisk out from the centre.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Drink straight away, before the powder settles. For a milder, longer drink, stir in up to 120 ml more 80 °C water after whisking.

tips: Soak a bamboo whisk in warm water for a minute first so the tines are supple.
Ceremonial-grade matcha is sweeter and greener; culinary grade is better for lattes and baking.
Keep matcha sealed in the fridge; it loses colour and flavour quickly once opened.
Whisk from the wrist, not the arm, keeping the whisk just off the bottom of the bowl.
storage: Best made and drunk at once; it doesn't keep. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
